question.text: Under SEBI regulations, what is the maximum Total Expense Ratio (TER) permitted for an equity-oriented mutual fund scheme on the first Rs. 500 crore of daily net assets?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A workbook (p145-p147), for open-ended equity-oriented schemes the TER slab on the first Rs. 500 crore of daily net assets is 2.25%, then 2.00% on the next Rs. 250 crore, and 1.75% on the next Rs. 1,250 crore (and further declining slabs at higher AUM). For other-than-equity (debt) schemes, the corresponding top-slab limit is 2.00% on the first Rs. 500 crore. The Trap: 1.75% and 1.50% are slab values applicable at higher AUM levels, not the first Rs. 500 crore. 2.50% is not the current first-slab limit for equity-oriented schemes under the workbook's TER table. Note: The slab structure rewards scale — as AUM grows, the marginal TER rate on incremental AUM falls, lowering the blended TER for investors in larger schemes.
